 WASHINGTON (TNND) — Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said Tuesday that over $1 million in alleged SNAP fraud was uncovered at a convenience store in Michigan.
 “Mohinder Singh, operator of Romario’s Party Store in Lansing, was indicted on one count of theft of public money and nine counts of SNAP fraud,” Rollins wrote in a post on the social media platform, X. 
 View post on X 
 The indictment alleges that Singh illegally exchanged cash and other items for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits with his customers.
 “Additionally, it is alleged that Singh charged a fee payable in SNAP benefits after extending credit to some of his customers,” the Department of Justice put out in a press release . “The government alleged that Singh intended more than $1 million in loss to the government.” 
 If he is convicted, he could face up to 10 years in prison.
 “These schemes siphoned millions from taxpayers and robbed struggling Americans of the benefits they depend on so fraudsters could use them for own selfish purposes,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement. “Through our partnership with the Department of Agriculture, this nationwide surge exposed and disrupted criminal networks that targeted vulnerable American families. The Department of Justice will continue working to root out fraud in every federal agency and program.” 
 Rollins encouraged Americans to report SNAP fraud if they see something and posted a link for people to use if they have something to report.
